findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` as its first argument, but the eligibility check passes the closure variable `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)`. In the dashboard-widget split path (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is deliberately invoked with a different dataset (e.g. `discover` for the errors-only/transactions-only probe queries) while the outer `dataset` is still the originally requested one (e.g. `metrics_enhanced_performance`). As a result the upsampling decision is computed for a dataset that is not the one being queried: upsampling is silently skipped for the split errors query (under-reported counts for allowlisted projects) and could conversely be applied to a dataset whose query builder has no `upsampled_count` function. The check should use `scoped_dataset`.

findings.title: `upsampled_count()` only registered for the discover dataset, but applied to the errors dataset
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is added only to `DiscoverDatasetConfig.function_converter`, yet `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` returns `True` unconditionally when `dataset is sentry.snuba.errors`. The errors dataset is resolved through its own `ErrorsDatasetConfig` function registry, which does not contain `upsampled_count`, so any `yAxis=count()` request with `dataset=errors` for allowlisted projects will be rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count` and then fail with an "is not a valid function" search error instead of returning data. There is also no test exercising `dataset=errors`, so this path is completely uncovered.

findings.title: `_is_error_focused_query` substring match also matches negated error queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does `"event.type:error" in query`. This matches `!event.type:error` (a query that explicitly excludes errors, i.e. transactions) as well as occurrences inside quoted free-text/message filters. For such queries the discover `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()` (`sum(sample_weight)`), producing wrong (or null/zero) numbers for non-error rows where `sample_weight` is absent. The check needs to parse the query (or at least exclude negations) rather than do a raw substring test.

findings.title: Error-focus detection reads `request.GET['query']` instead of the query actually executed
findings.body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` / `_is_error_focused_query` inspect the raw `request.GET["query"]`, but `_get_event_stats` is frequently called with a *modified* query string: the dashboard widget split path builds `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` (errors-only) and `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"` (transactions-only). Because the helper never sees these, the errors-only probe query is not recognized as error-focused (upsampling skipped, counts under-reported) while the transactions-only query inherits the decision made from the original request. The query string that is actually executed should be passed into the helper.

findings.title: 60s eligibility cache has no working invalidation; option changes are ignored and the cache adds little value
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist decision for 60 seconds keyed by org + project ids. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined to clear it but is never called from anywhere in the codebase, and it requires knowing the exact project-id set used in the cache key, so it cannot realistically invalidate all affected entries when `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` changes. Consequence: adding or (more importantly) removing a project from the allowlist — e.g. to stop emitting inflated counts during an incident — takes effect only after up to 60s, with no way to force it. Note also that `options.get` is already backed by the options cache, so the extra caching layer buys little while introducing this staleness and a stale-data risk. The surrounding docstring claiming "we always have the latest configuration state" contradicts the caching behaviour.

findings.title: Cache key built from Python `hash()` of project ids can collide
findings.body: The cache key is `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}"`. Using an opaque 64-bit hash instead of the sorted ids themselves means two different project sets in the same organization can map to the same key, in which case one set inherits the other's eligibility verdict and the returned counts are silently wrong (either inflated or not upsampled). Since this cache is shared across processes, the wrong value is served broadly. Serialize the sorted ids (or a stable digest with low collision risk) into the key instead.

findings.title: `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` can yield NULL and is exposed as a public function
findings.body: Two problems with the new `upsampled_count` SnQL function: (1) `sample_weight` is not guaranteed to be populated for all error rows in an allowlisted project (events ingested before the feature was enabled, or SDKs not sending `contexts.error_sampling`); for a nullable column ClickHouse `sum` over all-NULL rows returns NULL, and `toInt64` of that stays NULL, so the timeseries can return `null` counts where consumers (zerofill, frontend charts, alert comparisons) expect integers. The docstring's assumption that "sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects" is not enforced anywhere — consider `ifNull(...)`/`sumIf` semantics. (2) Unlike the neighbouring internal helpers, it is not marked `private=True`, so any user can request `yAxis=upsampled_count()` on discover for non-allowlisted projects and get meaningless zero/null results, a new public API surface that was presumably not intended.

findings.title: Test factory fabricates `sample_rate` and silently swallows all errors
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` injects `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` in `store_event`, bypassing the real ingest path (relay/event manager) that is responsible for deriving the sampling weight in production. The new endpoint tests therefore validate upsampled counts against a value the test harness itself invents, so a regression in the real normalization/ingest logic would not be caught. Additionally both `try/except Exception: pass` blocks hide genuine problems (e.g. a non-numeric `client_sample_rate`), silently producing events without a sample rate and turning a meaningful assertion failure into a confusing count mismatch.

findings.title: Stray git submodule entry `sentry-repo` committed
findings.body: The PR adds a gitlink (`Subproject commit a5d2909...`) at path `sentry-repo` with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This is clearly an accidental artifact of local tooling: it pollutes the repository tree, makes `git submodule status/update` and some clone/CI tooling report errors for an unregistered submodule, and pins a commit of the repository inside itself. It should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: Misleading comments on upsampled count assertions
findings.body: `assert data[0][1][0]["count"] == 10  # First bucket has 1 event` (and the following line) claim the bucket contains 1 event while asserting a count of 10. The value 10 is the upsampled count (1 event at a 0.1 client sample rate); the comment makes the assertion look wrong and will mislead the next person debugging a failure here. State that the raw event count is 1 and the expected upsampled count is 10.

findings.title: `setUp` overwrites `self.user` after `login_as`, and no coverage for errors dataset / caching
findings.body: In the new `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest.setUp`, `self.user` is reassigned to a freshly created user after `self.login_as(user=self.user)`, so `self.user` no longer refers to the authenticated user; any later use of `self.user` for auth assertions in this class would be wrong (the workaround `self.authed_user` hints at the confusion). The class also lacks tests for the two riskiest new behaviours: requests with `dataset=errors` (where `upsampled_count()` is applied unconditionally) and the newly added 60-second eligibility cache (stale allowlist results), both of which are currently unverified.
